Metastasi osteoblastiche vertebrali mult: Multiple osteoblastic vertebral metastases from prostate carcinoma (T3-T5, T7-T8, L2-L3)
Uomo di 74 anni con carcinoma della pros: 74-year-old man with prostate carcinoma. Non-contrast CT performed for radiotherapy planning (reformatted at 2 mm). Use the bone window and sagittal reformats (MPR).
Referta in ordine: tecnica, rachide, con: Report in order: technique, spine, conclusion.
Le metastasi osteoblastiche (sclerotiche:
Osteoblastic (sclerotic) metastases are typical of prostate carcinoma; other frequent primaries are breast (often mixed), carcinoid and lymphoma. On CT they appear as dense areas, focal or diffuse up to the “ivory vertebra”.
Differential diagnosis of the ivory vertebra: osteoblastic metastasis, lymphoma, Paget (enlarged vertebra with thickened cortex, “picture-frame” appearance). Bone islands are small, well-defined, with brush-like margins and very high density (generally > 885 HU), and do not increase in number.
In the report: levels involved, involvement of the posterior elements, pathologic fractures, canal compromise (risk of cord compression) and stability (SINS score). For staging: bone scintigraphy or PSMA PET.
Vertebre sclerotiche multiple in un uomo: Multiple sclerotic vertebrae in an older man: prostate metastases until proven otherwise.
Carcinoma prostatico con metastasi osteo: Prostate carcinoma with osteoblastic metastases at T3, T4, T5, T7, T8, L2 and L3 (Spine-Mets-CT-SEG clinical data). Lesions at T7 in the posterior elements, at T3 in the pars, at T8 in the superior endplate.
